title: Determination of blood cell gene expression profiles during early life of premature infants who develop bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD)
description: To investigate early blood biomarkers of BPD development, RNA from cord blood cells or peripheral blood cells of premature infants was subjected to RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) and data were analyzed with 9 covariates including gestational age (GA), sex, birth weight (BW), estimated CD4+T cell%, CD8+T cell%, B cell%, monocyte%, granulocyte%, and nucleated red blood cell (NRBC)%. The effect of prolonged oxygen (>14 days O2) treatment in newborn intensive care unit on blood cell transcriptome was determined among nonBPD preterm infants. Overall design: Differential gene expression profiles were determined by RNA-seq of two independent analyses in an Argentina preterm infant cohort : Analysis 1- Two treatment groups, BPD and nonBPD, at three time points (cord blood, postnatal day 14, and postnatal day 28), Analysis 2 - Two O2 treatment level groups (no-O2 vs High-O2) were compared among nonBPD neonates on postnatal day 14.

study_labels.evidence: The effect of prolonged oxygen (>14 days O2) treatment in newborn intensive care unit on blood cell transcriptome was determined among nonBPD preterm infants.
